investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled, does the NewRaft configuration scan still load every committed configuration entry at or below the commit index the node recovers, so that r.configurations reflects committed membership after restart?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the recovered commit index, and the scan loop starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so committed configuration entries at or below the commit index are never loaded into r.configurations; a restarted node keeps the snapshot configuration only, or an empty configuration when it has no snapshot.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the same gap and its consequences appear with commit-tracking log stores backed by production storage rather than the in-memory stores used in every measurement, and whether such a store's staging semantics change when the recovered commit index reaches a configuration entry; the cadence direction is measured in both directions, so what remains is store implementation breadth.

Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs clamps the store's commit index, applies the rec [preview: 924 characters omitted; see full record]
counterevidence: The negative control shows the gap is conditional, not universal: when the node's snapshot already covers the change, the restart recovers the configuration in force.
Both repair paths are measured: an arriving configuration entry restores the full set while the node is still a member, and an installed snapshot restores it when log replication is impossible.
The gap reproduces for a commit-tracking store that is also marked monotonic, which excludes the captured store's indexing shape as the cause but does not speak to production store implementations.
limitations: Applies to nodes configured with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, lastApplied equals the snapshot index and the scan range is unchanged.
All measurements use in-memory stores (including a hand-built monotonic commit-tracking store) with the repository's in-memory transport and mock FSM; production stores are not measured.

The installed-snapshot repair needed the leader's log to have been compacted past the node's last index, which the probe arranged by letting the cluster commit eighty entries while the node was down; other ways of reaching that state are not measured.

investigations.question: Can restoreFromCommittedLogs block NewRaft forever when the recovered committed range needs more FSM batches than the fsmMutateCh buffer, given that runFSM is only started after NewRaft's recovery completes?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs sends commitTuple batches through a 128-slot fsmMutateCh while no consumer exists yet, so a recovered committed range larger than 128 batches (64 entries each by default) makes NewRaft block indefinitely.
investigations.discriminator: Restart with RestoreCommittedLogs and a recovered committed range larger than 128*MaxAppendEntries entries, and observe whether NewRaft returns within a bounded interval.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Current account: a RestoreCommittedLogs restart cannot complete startup recovery once the recovered committed range needs more FSM batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh, because runFSM is only started after the recovery work that feeds it. The receipt shows both the boundary and the mechanism. Parsed event 3 (variant committed-range-entries-6001, 94 batches): NewRaft returned in 6 ms with lastAppl [preview: 1243 characters omitted; see full record]
counterevidence: The observation is a 20000 ms bounded wait, so the account claims a blocked startup under the stated conditions, not an infinite block proven for all time; a caller that closes the instance's shutdown channel could release the select.

The two cases differ only in the amount of authored history (6000 versus 9000 commands) and used a single-node in-memory cluster with an InmemCommitTrackingStore and snapshotting disabled, so the boundary is a batch-capacity property of NewRaft rather than a measured property of production stores.

The blocked range here was recovered from the same node's own log without any snapshot; whether a production restart reaches a range above 8192 entries depends on snapshot cadence and crash timing, which were not measured.
limitations: Applies only when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, NewRaft never calls processLogs before starting runFSM.
The threshold is expressed in MaxAppendEntries-sized batches against the 128-slot buffer, so a configuration with a different MaxAppendEntries moves the boundary proportionally.
Interaction with the configuration-scan gap (both appear in the same recovery sequence) is not separated by this experiment; each is independently witnessed.

investigations.hypothesis: GetConfiguration builds a fresh configurationsFuture whose configurations value carries only the latest Configuration, so its latestIndex stays zero: ConfigurationFuture.Index() always returns 0 and Stats copies that 0 into latest_configuration_index even though the node has a committed configuration entry with a real index.

No consensus decision, election, quorum or write outcome depends on this value, so the impact is confined to client-visible reporting.
